h: Abbeys, Moors and Steam Trains Around Helmsley
p: Flying displays are the heartbeat of a visit here, so check the times on arrival and plan the rest of your wander around them. Find a spot with a clear view and keep the camera on burst mode, because the birds move fast. Weather plays its part: birds of prey are wonderful on a still, bright day, while breezier conditions can bring out different flying styles. Either way, you'll learn something new about how these hunters work.

Helmsley is surrounded by gems. Rievaulx Abbey, a few miles up the valley and cared for by English Heritage, is among the most beautiful monastic ruins in England, and the setting alone makes it worth the trip. Above it sits Rievaulx Terrace, a National Trust grass terrace with temples and views down onto the abbey. Walkers might know that the Cleveland Way, a national trail that loops over the moors and down the coast, starts right in Helmsley, so even a short stretch makes for a lovely stroll.

A little further east, Hutton-le-Hole is home to the Ryedale Folk Museum, with historic buildings rescued from around the moors and rebuilt in the village. Pickering is the base of the North Yorkshire Moors Railway, where you can take a steam train through the dales towards Goathland and Whitby. Castle Howard, the grand stately home near Malton, is also within easy reach for a day of house and gardens. Base yourself in Helmsley for a few nights and you could fill a week without repeating yourself.
